predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: the former Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata as far as the Junta of 25 May 1810 held it: Buenos Aires and the Argentine provinces, with the Banda Oriental in revolt against Montevideo

successors.name: Argentine Confederation
successors.text: the Argentine provinces under the Federal Pact of 4 January 1831; the page: 'It was the name of the country from 1831 to 1852'

successors.name: Federal League
successors.text: Entre Ríos, Corrientes, Misiones, Santa Fe, Córdoba and the Eastern Province, 1815-1820

successors.name: Paraguay
successors.text: Paraguay, whose independence the treaty of 12 October 1811 acknowledged

successors.name: Oriental Republic of Uruguay
successors.text: the Eastern Bank, 'an independent state' in 1828 after British intervention (Montevideo Treaty of 28 August 1828)

successors.name: Bolivia
successors.text: Upper Peru, which 'was never retaken, and became Bolivia years later'; infobox 'Succeeded by: 1825 Upper Peru'

ledger.x: 25 May 1810: the Primera Junta takes power at Buenos Aires.
1811: the first campaign into Upper Peru.
28 February 1811: the Cry of Asencio begins the Oriental Revolution.
12 October 1811: the first treaty acknowledges Paraguay's independence.
22 November 1811: the First Triumvirate adopts 'United Provinces of the Río de la Plata'.
20-23 June 1814: Montevideo falls to Buenos Aires.
1815: the provinces of the Federal League leave Buenos Aires.
10 January 1815: Guayabos brings the Eastern Bank into the Federal League.
29 November 1815: Viluma ends the Upper Peru campaigns.
9 July 1816: the Congress of Tucumán declares independence.
1 February 1820: Cepeda ends the Federal League's separate existence.
29 September 1820: Ramírez founds the Republic of Entre Ríos.
28 September 1821: Entre Ríos returns to the provincial alliance.
12 October 1821: Corrientes declares itself an autonomous federated province.
25 October 1825: the Argentine Congress takes in the Banda Oriental.
27 August 1828: the Preliminary Peace Convention makes Uruguay independent.

wars.name: Paraguay campaign
wars.outcome: Buenos Aires' expedition 'was defeated'; the treaty of 12 October 1811 acknowledged Paraguay's independence.

wars.name: Upper Peru campaigns
wars.outcome: The first campaign failed after Huaqui (20 June 1811) and Rondeau was defeated at Viluma on 29 November 1815; Upper Peru stayed royalist and became Bolivia.

wars.name: Oriental Revolution and the sieges of Montevideo
wars.outcome: Cry of Asencio 28 February 1811; the October 1811 treaty acknowledged the viceroy's authority over the Eastern Bank; the Second Siege began in September 1812; Vigodet surrendered on 20 June 1814 and Alvear occupied Montevideo on 23 June.

wars.name: Battle of Cepeda (1820)
wars.outcome: The Federals (Santa Fe, Entre Ríos) defeated the national government under Supreme Director Rondeau on 1 February 1820; the Treaty of Pilar followed on 23 February; the League ended and the caudillo era began.

wars.name: Cisplatine War
wars.outcome: Brazil declared war on 10 December 1825; there was fighting at Sarandí (12 October 1825) and Ituzaingó/Passo do Rosário (20 February 1827), the Argentines defeated the Brazilian flotilla at Juncal and the Brazilian blockade of Buenos Aires caused 'severe…

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line fixes any frontier of the United Provinces on land: the Andean, Chaco, Patagonian and Banda Oriental limits are approximate, and from 1820 to 1826 the page calls the state 'a loose alliance of autonomous provinces'.
